decisions.name: Evidence completion bound: anchor and window
decisions.statement: The ExecutionReceipt's evidence_complete_by_utc derives as anchor + window. The anchor is the attempt's CANDIDATE_FROZEN instant — the t-a05 TransitionRecord's recorded_utc, equal by construction to the attempt row's updated_utc while the attempt remains CANDIDATE_FROZEN (the only transition into that state, and receipt admission is only possible in it). The window is evidence_collection_window_seconds, a D-18 configuration default (default 3600, integer seconds per D-28; effective value = the stricter of delegation or repository policy and operational config, carried as collector configuration in v1). The derivation is recorded inside the receipt's derivation block {rule, anchor_utc, window_seconds}, so every bound is auditable from the receipt alone and re-derivable from the ledger.
basis: RECONCILIATION M2 addendum: the bound's derivation from admission facts is Chapter 3's receipt semantics

decisions.name: Receipt authority is derived, never declared
decisions.statement: admit_execution_receipt re-derives the entire canonical receipt payload from durable ledger facts (the frozen record's evidence_requirements, the attempt's dispatched role, the attempt_witnesses rows, the D-66 store probe, the D-C3-1 anchor) plus exactly one collector-supplied parameter (the window, validated as a D-28 uint >= 1) and admits the submitted bytes only when they are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the re-derivation. A receipt therefore cannot declare any classification, bound, witness set or role fact the ledger does not support: forging any field changes the bytes and the admission is refused. The admitted row's completeness and evidence_complete_by_utc are the only inputs t-a06/t-s09 (execution_receipt_complete) and t-a13/t-s45 (execution_receipt_integrity_failed_or_incomplete_beyond_bound) consume.

decisions.name: INTEGRITY_FAILED classification and the D-66 interplay
decisions.statement: The collector classifies INTEGRITY_FAILED when an admitted witness row's bytes are missing from the content store or no longer re-hash to their admitted address, probed non-raising at collection (store.verify). t-a13 then fails the candidate and t-s45 halts the sequence by REGISTERED transitions in one transaction, durably blocking acceptance (INV-23) in the running session. The same corruption independently halts the next recover() at its D-66 witness re-hash: both behaviors are fail-closed and deliberate — a store that lost admitted evidence requires the operator, and no receipt, transition or recovery ever trusts or replaces the bytes.
basis: t-s45 source: Phase C finding (no exit for INTEGRITY_FAILED before verification)

decisions.name: Provider outcome vocabulary and the frozen mapping
decisions.statement: The AutoSwarm provider emits exactly three TERMINAL result outcomes - completed, failed, cancelled (runner.py: the result record initializes failed; cancelled on an observed cancel; completed only on success-exit with terminal output and no error). A result record with a recognized terminal outcome proves that provider-reported terminal outcome. An ABSENT result record proves only that no terminal provider outcome has been observed - NEVER that the call is running: a process may have died, the provider may have crashed between state writes, recovery may see an incomplete call directory. Running, stale or interrupted status comes only from separate durable lifecycle/session evidence (the t-a03 handle/session witnesses; staleness is the caller's t-a12 member lease) - absence of an authoritative observation is not an observation of the opposite state, the same G3 rule that keeps find_session None from proving launch failure. The frozen transport mapping normalizes completed -> success and passes failed and cancelled through verbatim; ANY unrecognized provider string also passes through verbatim and can satisfy a role only if the frozen completion_policies.success_outcomes lists it. The provider reports; the frozen contract decides (U-06 resolved 2026-11-12 from the provider source and the 19 retained result records; the missing-result semantics corrected by the operator's pre-commit review).

decisions.name: Raw witness trust model: exact bytes, tolerant recognition
decisions.statement: Producer witness bytes are admitted exactly as produced (SHA-256 of the exact bytes is the identity; no canonicalization, rewriting, stripping, normalization or inferred fields - unknown keys, nulls and provider metadata are preserved). Parsing is tolerant and exists only to extract RECOGNIZED correlation facts per registered kind; unrecognized or unparseable bytes admit normally and contribute no facts. A recognized fact that names an execution identity contradicting the ledger's bound call refuses admission; a recognized fact may inform joins and classification; an unknown field grants nothing. Protocol structures minted FROM witnesses (the obj-15 entries, causal_joins, provenance rows) follow normal canonical rules.
basis: the live provider record family (task/handle/result; the governance evidence record; the session rollout)

decisions.name: Causal joins: controller rule and the DENY-then-ran contradiction
decisions.statement: The child-parent causal join is the provider task record's controller_id, guaranteed by the provider contract (prepare stamps it, creation refuses without it, the runner hard-indexes it; 19/19 retained records well-formed; U-07 resolved): shape (call|main)_[a-f0-9]{32}, where call_* controllers chain to their own task records and main_* anchors a host session outside the attempt graph. Joins derive only from ledger facts and recognized witness facts - never from directory timestamps, process timing, newest-file order or string similarity. Missing identity facts classify as missing evidence (INCOMPLETE under the D-C3-1 bound); facts proving an impossible or forbidden relationship classify as contradictions (INTEGRITY_FAILED), among them deny_then_ran: a governance DENY for (command_sha256 S, session N) joined by content hash and session identity - never wall-clock proximity - to evidence that a command with sha S executed in session N (U-01's deterministic detection rule; the historical root cause stays a Helios-side item). When a decision or execution record names NO session, the join falls back to the attempt's own admitted set - attempt-scoped, still content-hash-keyed, never time-keyed - because every admitted governance record already passed the admission identity gate.

decisions.name: INDEX_LAG is a collector diagnostic that cannot become authority
decisions.statement: cap-30's 'index state' facet is the Collector's index_state surface: an INJECTED catalog probe (the registered hdb -> collector authority edge is labeled 'index, INDEX_LAG diagnostic only'; cap-28 grants the collector R) whose status document is recognized tolerantly the witness-facts way - watermarks.latest_committed_utc / latest_observed_utc, integrity.closed, schema; an absent probe, a failing probe and an unrecognized document each REPORT a diagnostic state and never raise. For a frozen attempt the committed watermark is compared against the newest admitted evidence instant to report INDEX_LAG. The structural guarantee: the obj-15 payload is a pure function of durable ledger facts re-derived byte-identically by the collector, the admission seam and recovery (D-C3-2), so a live probe result CANNOT enter the receipt, a transition precondition or a classification without breaking that equality - INDEX_LAG never blocks, and no frozen v1 assertion can declare an HDB-derived query (the contract schema names none). Proven by CH3-index-lag-diagnostic, including the source scan that keeps the derivation, the seam and the intelligence plane blind to the index surface.

decisions.name: The D-12 integrity classes over admitted governance facts
decisions.statement: Within one attempt's admitted obj-12 set, a record proving a command EXECUTED (hook_event PostToolUse, or success true) with no recorded decision for it anywhere in the set is the contradiction execution_without_decision: D-12's 'orphan' and 'execution with no recorded decision' are one mechanical rule, joined by tool_use_id when the execution record carries one, else by command content hash and session identity (equal or either absent, the D-C3-6 containment) - never wall-clock. The rule is a POSITIVE observation of a fail-open: the governance record family guarantees a decision precedes execution, so the execution record itself proves the governance chain broke - this is never an inference from mere absence of evidence (the G3 principle stands). A record carrying both its decision and its execution facts is decided by itself; a DENY record that also proves the execution joins ITSELF as deny_then_ran (F-C3-9: the original elif dropped the one-record case); an enforced DENY with no execution classifies NOTHING - DENY counts are diagnostic, visible in the admitted facts and causal joins, never in the classification. Contradictions classify INTEGRITY_FAILED (INV-68). Proven by CH3-integrity-classes.

decisions.name: Specification inputs re-hash at dispatch and at collection
decisions.statement: The frozen record's specification_inputs.name_to_exact_byte_sha256 declares the exact input bytes. t-a02 (dispatch_attempt) refuses dispatch when any declared input no longer resolves to its declared bytes - fail closed BEFORE any external launch, where repair is still possible. Collection re-probes every declared input non-raising (store.verify, the D-66 pattern) and the receipt ALWAYS binds the result as input_rehash (the chapter-1 obj-15 always-binding), {} when the record declares none; any non-intact input classifies INTEGRITY_FAILED (INV-37: a change is INTEGRITY_FAILED; bytes missing under a declared address are the same fail-closed class as D-C3-3's witnesses). The admission seam and recovery 8f re-derive input_rehash byte-identically with the rest of the payload; recovery independently halts EARLIER, at the records loop, when a frozen input no longer resolves - the same deliberate interplay D-C3-3 records: both arms fail closed, and the operator owns the store. Proven by CH3-input-rehash.
basis: chapter-1 phase-a inventory: the input_rehash binding

enforcement_notes: cap-30 enforcement is 'interim: code' per capabilities.json: the Collector component (principal 'collector', the registered obj-15 minter) is the only code path that mints and submits receipts; the Taskforce (forbidden on cap-30) only asks the collector to collect. The admission seam additionally refuses any payload whose minter is not the registered obj-15 minter, so a forged principal fails structurally before the byte-equality check. The ipc_acl target enforcement stays with the later process-separation milestone.
